result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick the 'I'm not creative' angle for good reasons, use the brief's facts accurately and show 31 of 46 as about two-thirds. B shows the idea in three forms (an email, a door sign and a week-two message), names a clear fallback, and correctly flags that Oct 21 has already passed. A shows the idea mainly as one sample ad, wrongly assumes Oct 21 is next week, and suggests alternatives without naming a single fallback. B's door sign makes a claim that may not be true yet, but B says to check it before using it. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers build their pick on the 'I'm not creative' hesitation and use the brief's facts accurately. A shows the idea in three forms (a reply post or email, a street-door sign and a week-two student message) and gives a clear plain fallback, while B gives headline ideas and a single sample ad with no named fallback. B also adds an unsupported claim that 'most pottery classes make you wait'. Its sample ad places the 'not creative' line right before the 31-of-46 figure, which loosely implies those were the people who returned, even though B warns against that.
